DESCRIPTION: Cited additive library for science toolkit compounding screens.

records.name: Joncryl ADR-4468 (epoxy styrene-acrylic)

chemistry.value: styrene-acrylic copolymer with glycidyl methacrylate epoxy groups

antagonisms: sodium carboxylates (Na benzoate, Na montanate) catalyse epoxy ring-opening homopolymerisation
acidic phosphorus compounds (DOPO, phosphites hydrolysed to acids) consume epoxy
moisture hydrolyses epoxy groups
excess epoxy gels the melt (see gel point)

food_contact.value: not cleared for food contact in all jurisdictions; confirm grade

records.mechanism: Multi-epoxy oligomer couples COOH (and OH) chain ends: one molecule can couple several chains, raising Mn and restoring IV. Dose is gel-limited.
records.notes: EEW 310 and fw = Mw/EEW ~23.4 match the rPET engine; confirm on the BASF datasheet.

records.name: PMDA (pyromellitic dianhydride)
antagonisms: hydrolyses to pyromellitic acid in moist melt
anhydride + OH opens to COOH which can re-esterify
records.mechanism: One PMDA opens two anhydride rings toward two OH ends (functionality 4), coupling chains. EEW = Mw/2 = 109.06 g/mol.

records.name: PBO (1,3-phenylene-bis(2-oxazoline))
antagonisms: oxazoline hydrolyses slowly in moist conditions
records.mechanism: Oxazoline ring opens selectively on COOH (no gel risk, functionality 2); used for PET/PA chain extension.

records.name: Stabaxol P (polymeric carbodiimide)
antagonisms: consumes water but also reacts with COOH; overdosing deactivates acid ends
records.mechanism: Carbodiimide scavenges water and COOH, blocking hydrolysis; also a chain extender for polyesters/polyamides.

records.name: TDI dimer/trimer isocyanate extender
antagonisms: NCO reacts with water to CO2 (foaming) and urea; moisture must be excluded
records.mechanism: NCO couples OH/NH2 ends; very moisture-sensitive, rarely used in PET.

records.name: Irganox 1010 (hindered phenol)
antagonisms: hindered phenol is consumed by acid; add phosphite synergist
records.mechanism: Donates H to alkylperoxyl radicals, breaking the oxidative chain. Standard primary AO.

records.name: Irgafos 168 (phosphite)
antagonisms: hydrolyses to phenol + phosphoric acid in moist melt (acid catalyses polyester hydrolysis and consumes epoxy)
records.mechanism: Reduces hydroperoxides to alcohols; protects colour during processing. Hydrolysis-sensitive.

records.name: DSTDP (distearyl thiodipropionate)
antagonisms: sulfur odour at high temperature
thioester + hindered phenol is a classic synergist pair
records.mechanism: Thioether decomposes hydroperoxides; long-term thermal stabiliser, synergises with hindered phenols.

records.name: BHT (2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenol)
antagonisms: volatile above ~200 C (loss at melt temperatures)
records.mechanism: Low-MW hindered phenol; cheap but migrates and volatilises in high-temperature processing.

records.name: Tinuvin 770 (HALS)
antagonisms: basic amine can catalyse polyester hydrolysis / interfere with epoxy in PET
records.mechanism: Cyclic regeneration of nitroxyl radical scavenges photo-oxidation; does not absorb UV.

records.name: Tinuvin 326 (benzotriazole)
antagonisms: none major
records.mechanism: Absorbs UV and dissipates as heat; protects colour and surface gloss.

records.name: Talc (nucleating grade)
antagonisms: platelet stiffens and nucleates; lowers clarity
records.mechanism: High-surface-area platelets nucleate crystallisation (heterogeneous). Doubles as a stiffening filler.

records.name: Sodium benzoate

chemistry.value: C7H5NaO2 sodium salt of benzoic acid

antagonisms: sodium carboxylate catalyses epoxy ring-opening (incompatible with epoxy chain extenders)
records.mechanism: Classic PP/PET nucleating agent; the carboxylate is also an epoxy-cure catalyst, a key antagonism.

records.name: Sodium montanate

chemistry.value: sodium salt of montan-wax long-chain carboxylic acids

antagonisms: sodium carboxylate catalyses epoxy ring-opening (incompatible with epoxy chain extenders)
records.mechanism: Efficient PET nucleator; carboxylate/epoxy antagonism is the reason rPET routes pair it with the extender cautiously.

records.name: Millad 3988 (dibenzylidene sorbitol)
antagonisms: excess or overheating causes plate-out and haze
records.mechanism: Dissolves in PP melt and re-precipitates as a nanofibrillar network that clarifies by refining spherulites.

records.name: NA-11 (sodium phosphate ester nucleator)
antagonisms: acidic hydrolysis products can interact with basic additives
records.mechanism: Organophosphate nucleator giving high PP crystallisation temperature and improved stiffness.

records.name: NPG dibenzoate
antagonisms: lowers Tg/Tm and modulus; not for food contact
records.mechanism: Lowers PET Tg enough to crystallise in a 90-100 C water-heated mould (rPET route A).

records.name: ATBC (acetyl tributyl citrate)
antagonisms: high loadings plasticise the matrix and drop HDT
records.mechanism: Phthalate-free food-contact plasticiser; replaces DOP/DEHP.

records.name: DBS (dibutyl sebacate)
antagonisms: limited compatibility with nonpolar polyolefins
records.mechanism: Phthalate-free low-temperature plasticiser.

records.name: Triacetin (glycerol triacetate)
antagonisms: volatile at high temperature (bp ~258 C)
records.mechanism: Food-contact (GRAS) plasticiser; also used as a PLA melt-plasticiser.

records.name: Lotader AX (E-MA-GMA terpolymer)

chemistry.value: ethylene - methyl acrylate - glycidyl methacrylate random terpolymer

antagonisms: GMA epoxy contributes to the epoxy:COOH stoichiometry (raises gel risk)
food-contact grade required for food use
records.mechanism: GMA grafts epoxy reactivity onto a rubbery ethylene backbone; toughens and compatibilises. EEW from 8 % GMA: 142.15/0.08 = 1777 g/mol.

records.name: MBS core-shell
antagonisms: butadiene lowers UV/thermal stability
not for transparent high-clarity parts (refractive mismatch)
records.mechanism: Core-shell rubber toughens glassy matrices (PC, PVC) with minimal modulus loss.

records.name: SEBS-g-MA

chemistry.value: styrene-ethylene/butylene-styrene block copolymer grafted with maleic anhydride

antagonisms: anhydride hydrolyses in moist conditions
records.mechanism: Maleated rubber toughens PA and improves PA/PP blends.

records.name: EPDM-g-MA

chemistry.value: ethylene-propylene-diene rubber grafted with maleic anhydride

antagonisms: anhydride hydrolyses in moist conditions
records.mechanism: Maleated EPDM is the standard PP and PA toughener.

records.name: PP-g-MA (maleated PP)
antagonisms: excess maleic anhydride can yellow
records.mechanism: Couples PP to glass fibre sizing and to PA in blends.

records.name: PETS (pentaerythritol tetrastearate)
antagonisms: overdosing causes plate-out and weld-line weakness
records.mechanism: External lubricant/release; low volatility ester wax.

records.name: EBS (ethylene bis stearamide)
antagonisms: overdosing causes plate-out
records.mechanism: Internal/external lubricant and pigment dispersant.

records.name: Calcium stearate

chemistry.value: C36H70CaO4 calcium salt of stearic acid

antagonisms: metal stearates can catalyse degradation in polyesters/polyamides at high loading
records.mechanism: Neutralises residual acid catalyst; internal lubricant.

records.name: Zinc stearate

chemistry.value: C36H70O4Zn zinc salt of stearic acid

antagonisms: zinc stearate catalyses PVC dehydrochlorination
metal stearate + epoxy antagonism at high loading
records.mechanism: Internal/external lubricant; strong release effect at low dose.

records.name: DOPO (9,10-dihydro-9-oxa-10-phosphaphenanthrene-10-oxide)
antagonisms: acidic P-H consumes epoxy (competes with chain extender)
phosphorus lowers thermal stability
records.mechanism: Reactive phosphorus flame retardant; P-H adds across oxirane to graft DOPO onto epoxy resins.

records.name: ATH (aluminium trihydroxide)
antagonisms: releases water above ~200 C (foaming/porosity at melt temps)
high loading kills mechanicals
records.mechanism: Endothermic dehydration to Al2O3 + 3H2O cools and dilutes the flame; needs 20-60 % loading.

records.name: MDH (magnesium dihydroxide)
antagonisms: dehydrates ~330 C (usable at higher temps than ATH)
high loading kills mechanicals
records.mechanism: Higher decomposition temperature than ATH; suitable for PA.

records.name: Exolit OP 1230 (Al diethylphosphinate)
antagonisms: phosphorus acid species can catalyse polyester hydrolysis in moist processing
records.mechanism: Halogen-free P-based FR for polyamides and polyesters; gas + condensed phase.

records.name: Melamine cyanurate
antagonisms: sublimes above ~320 C (plate-out, nozzle deposits)
records.mechanism: N-based FR for unfilled PA; endothermic decomposition and fuel dilution.

records.name: Anthranilamide (2-aminobenzamide)
antagonisms: reacts 1:1 with acetaldehyde (stoichiometric capacity, not kinetics)
records.mechanism: Primary amine condenses with acetaldehyde to an imine, trapping preform AA in PET. Capacity ~16 ppm AA per 50 ppm additive.

records.name: Optical brightener OB
antagonisms: none major
records.mechanism: Blue-emitting fluorophore masks yellow; dosage in the 10-500 ppm range.

records.name: GMS (glycerol monostearate)
antagonisms: migrates to surface (bloom); washes off
records.mechanism: Internal antistat: polar ester migrates to the surface and dissipates static charge.

records.name: Azodicarbonamide (ADCA)
antagonisms: decomposition residue (urazole) and semicarbazide are a food-contact concern
records.mechanism: Exothermic chemical blowing agent; decomposes to gases near processing temperature.

records.name: Sodium bicarbonate
antagonisms: releases CO2 + water (water is a hydrolysis risk in polyesters)
records.mechanism: Endothermic CBA; CO2 + H2O release cools the melt and foams it.

records.name: Triphenyl phosphite (TPP)
antagonisms: hydrolyses to phenol + phosphoric acid (acid consumes epoxy / catalyses polyester hydrolysis)
records.mechanism: Liquid phosphite secondary antioxidant; hydrolytically unstable.

records.name: Chimassorb 944 (oligomeric HALS)
antagonisms: basic amine can interfere with acid-catalysed polyester systems
records.mechanism: High-MW oligomeric HALS: low migration and extraction, long-term light stability.

records.name: Zinc borate
antagonisms: releases water on heating (porosity at high loading)
records.mechanism: Char-forming FR synergist (often with ATH/antimony); smoke suppressant.
